'''Leonard (Len) R Stephens''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of London|FRS]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org/people/leonard-stephens/ |title= |website=royalsociety.org |access-date=January 12, 2014}}{{title missing|date=May 2022}}</ref> (born 18 June 1960) is a [[molecular biologist]], senior group leader and associate director at the [[Babraham Institute]].

Len Stephens has contributed much to the understanding of [[Inositol lipids and phosphate|inositol lipids]] functions in eukaryotic cells, and in particular in [[Neutrophil granulocyte|neutrophils]]. Early highlights were the mapping of new pathways of inositol phosphate synthesis.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Stephens | first1 = L.R. | last2 = Hughes | first2 = K.T. | last3 = Irvine | first3 = R.F. | year = 1991 | title = Pathway of phosphatidylinositol(3,4,5)-trisphosphate synthesis in activated neutrophils | journal = Nature | volume = 351 | issue = 6321 | pages = 33–39 | doi=10.1038/351033a0| pmid = 1851250 | bibcode = 1991Natur.351...33S | s2cid = 12322154 }}</ref>
Together with his long-time collaborator [[Phillip Thomas Hawkins]], he established that [[Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate|PtdIns(4,5)P2]] is the main substrate of receptor-controlled Type 1 [[phosphoinositide 3-kinases]] (PI3Ks), thus identifying [[Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate|PtdIns(3,4,5)P3]] as the key output signal produced by this enzyme.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hawkins | first1 = P.T. | last2 = Jackson | first2 = T.R. | last3 = Stephens | first3 = L.R. | year = 1992 | title = Platelet-derived growth factor stimulates synthesis of Ptdlns(3,4,5)P3 by activating a Ptdlns(4,5)P2 3-OH kinase | journal = Nature | volume = 358 | issue = 6382 | pages = 157–159 | doi=10.1038/358157a0 | pmid=1319558| bibcode = 1992Natur.358..157H | s2cid = 4310878 }}</ref>
They identified and isolated the [[GPCR]]-activated Type 1B PI3K (PI3KΥ) and, in a sustained body of work, defined its structure, explained its complex pattern of regulation by GβΥ and [[Ras subfamily|Ras]], and proved its role in [[inflammation|inflammatory events]] ''in vivo''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Stephens | first1 = L. | last2 = Smrcka | first2 = A. | last3 = Cooke | first3 = F.T. | last4 = Jackson | first4 = T.R. | last5 = Sternweis | first5 = P.C. | last6 = Hawkins | first6 = P.T. | year = 1994 | title = A novel phosphoinositide 3 kinase activity in myeloid-derived cells is activated by G protein βγ subunits | journal = Cell | volume = 77 | issue = 1 | pages = 83–93 | doi=10.1016/0092-8674(94)90237-2 | pmid=8156600| s2cid = 53255676 }}</ref>
They – in parallel with [[Dario Alessi]] – identified [[phosphoinositide-dependent kinase-1]] as the PtdIns(3,4,5)P3-activated link between PI3K-1 activation and [[protein kinase B]] activation, a key pathway through which PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 formation regulates [[cell proliferation]] and survival.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Stephens | first1 = L.R. | last2 = Anderson | first2 = K. | last3 = Stokoe | first3 = D. | last4 = Erdjument-Bromage | first4 = H. | last5 = Painter | first5 = G.F. | last6 = Holmes | first6 = A.B. | last7 = Gaffney | first7 = P.R.J. | last8 = Reese | first8 = C.B. | last9 = McCormick | first9 = F. | last10 = Tempst | first10 = P. | last11 = Coadwell | first11 = J. | last12 = Hawkins | first12 = P.T. | year = 1998 | title = Protein Kinase B Kinases That Mediate Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-Trisphosphate-Dependent Activation of Protein Kinase B. | journal = Science | volume = 279 | issue = 5351 | pages = 710–714 | doi=10.1126/science.279.5351.710 | pmid=9445477| bibcode = 1998Sci...279..710S }}</ref> Later, they showed that PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 was responsible for the recruitment of both PKB and PDK1 to the membrane, and therefore the activation of the former by the latter.<ref>{{Cite journal

== Life ==

Len Stephens received a [[BSc]] in [[Biology]] (1981) and a [[PhD]] in [[Physiology]] (1984) from the [[University of Birmingham]]. After a post-doctoral training in S.K. & F. Research Ltd, he joined the AFRC IAPGR (now [[Babraham Institute]]). He became a staff scientist in the Inositide laboratory in 1992 and took the leadership of the laboratory in 1996. In 2008, he became associate director of the [[Babraham Institute]].

== Awards and recognition ==
Len Stephens has received several awards, including:
* 2011, elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society of London]]
* 2009, elected member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organisation]] (EMBO)
